Palo Alto & Stanford 25 places · area 1 of 7

  1. 1 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford · Japanese

    Ramen Nagi

    The Tokyo chain's first U.S. shop, famous for long nightly waits; the Original King is a silky 24-hour tonkotsu you customize by richness, garlic and a 1-to-10 spice scale.

    541 Bryant St, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Recommended by , , +1,

  2. 2 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford · Indian

    Eylan

    2026 Michelin Bib Gourmand and 2026 James Beard finalist for inventive regional Indian with a Californian twist; the flaky paratha-like flatbread stuffed with Dungeness crab is the standout. (On the Palo Alto/Menlo El Camino corridor.)

    500 El Camino Real, Suite 101, Menlo Park, CA 94025

    Recommended by , , +1,

  3. 3 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford · Indian

    Ettan

    Chef Srijith Gopinathan's Michelin Guide-listed 'Cal-Indian' dining room; the peas-and-ricotta stuffed kulcha with bright kale chutney is the signature.

    518 Bryant St, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Recommended by , ,

  4. 4 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford · American

    Oren's Hummus

    The University Avenue original of the beloved Israeli mini-chain, where silky made-daily hummus arrives warm topped with ful, mushrooms or lamb and mopped with fresh pita. A Palo Alto staple whose lines say it all.

    261 University Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Recommended by , ,

  5. 5 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Elizabeth F. Gamble Garden

    A historic 2.5-acre estate garden in downtown Palo Alto, with formal rose and perennial beds, a wisteria arbor and the 1902 Gamble family house. A quiet horticultural retreat open daily during daylight hours.

    Your guide’s note Grounds free and open every day at daylight; the Main House and offices keep weekday hours (roughly 9am-2pm). Donations encouraged.

    1431 Waverley St, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Recommended by ,

  6. 6 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Stanford Dish Loop

    An iconic ~3.7-mile paved loop over Stanford's rolling foothills, named for the giant radio telescope dish on the ridge, with sweeping views of the Bay and campus. A local exercise ritual dawn to dusk.

    Your guide’s note No dogs, no bikes; free street parking on Stanford Ave fills early on weekends. No water on the loop.

    Stanford Ave & Junipero Serra Blvd, Stanford, CA 94305

    Recommended by ,

  7. 7 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Baylands Nature Preserve

    One of the largest tracts of undisturbed marshland left on the Bay, with 15 miles of flat trails, boardwalks and superb birding along the salt marsh and sloughs. The Lucy Evans Interpretive Center sits at 2775 Embarcadero Rd.

    Your guide’s note Flat and stroller/bike friendly; best light and bird activity at sunrise and sunset.

    2500 Embarcadero Rd, Palo Alto, CA 94303

    Recommended by ,

  8. 8 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Cantor Arts Center

    Stanford's free art museum, whose 24-hour outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden holds some 20 monumental bronzes, one of the largest Rodin collections outside Paris, alongside wide-ranging galleries indoors.

    Your guide’s note Museum closed Tue-Wed; free. The Rodin Sculpture Garden is open outdoors 24/7, free.

    328 Lomita Dr, Stanford, CA 94305

    Recommended by ,

  9. 9 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Stanford Main Quad & Memorial Church

    The sandstone Romanesque heart of Stanford's campus, where the arcaded Main Quad frames Memorial Church, famed for its gold-leaf mosaic facade and stained glass, built by Jane Stanford in memory of Leland.

    Your guide’s note Free and open to the public; the Quad is walkable any time and the church is open daily outside services. Docent tours Fridays.

    450 Jane Stanford Way, Stanford, CA 94305

    Recommended by ,

  10. 10 Must see within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Cantor Arts Center & Rodin Sculpture Garden

    Stanford's free art museum spanning 5,000 years, holding the largest Rodin collection outside Paris - including a cast of The Gates of Hell - with an outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden open around the clock.

    Your guide’s note Free admission; museum closed Tuesdays. The outdoor sculpture garden is open 24/7 and lit at night.

    328 Lomita Dr, Stanford, CA 94305

    Recommended by ,

    Philz Coffee

  15. 15 Worth the detour within Palo Alto & Stanford

    HP Garage - Birthplace of Silicon Valley

    The one-car garage where Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard started Hewlett-Packard in 1939, widely honored as the birthplace of Silicon Valley. California Historical Landmark and on the National Register.

    Your guide’s note View from the public sidewalk ONLY. It is a private HP-owned property, not open inside; a bronze plaque on the front lawn reads 'Birthplace of Silicon Valley.' Viewable from the street/sidewalk only — no public interior access.

    367 Addison Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Recommended by ,

  16. 16 Worth the detour within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Foothills Nature Preserve

    A 1,400-acre Palo Alto nature preserve in the Santa Cruz Mountain foothills, with oak woodland trails, Boronda Lake and sweeping ridge views. Famous for being residents-only from 1969 until it finally opened to everyone in December 2020.

    Your guide’s note Now open to all; a small per-vehicle entry fee applies and the lot can fill on weekends. Open sunrise to sunset.

    3300 Page Mill Rd, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022

    Recommended by ,

  17. 17 Worth the detour within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Stanford Shopping Center

    An upscale open-air mall on El Camino Real at Sand Hill Road with 140-plus specialty stores from luxury brands to local favorites, adjoining the Stanford campus.

    Your guide’s note Free to enter; store hours vary. Ample free parking.

    660 Stanford Shopping Center, Palo Alto, CA 94304

    University Avenue (Downtown Palo Alto)

    The walkable spine of downtown Palo Alto, lined with boutiques, bookstores, cafes, art galleries, a cinema, and a dense run of restaurants a short walk from the Caltrain station.

    Your guide’s note Public street district, free to explore; shops and restaurants set their own hours. Street parking is tight at peak times; use the public garages.

    University Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94301

    Anderson Collection at Stanford University

    A purpose-built museum next to the Cantor housing the Anderson family's gift of postwar American painting, with major works by Pollock, Rothko, de Kooning, and Diebenkorn, all free to see.

    Palo Alto's beloved community donkeys graze a pasture beside the Bol Park bike path; one resident, Perry, was a live model for the Donkey character in Shrek.

    Anderson Collection at Stanford

    A jewel-box museum of postwar American modern and contemporary art - Pollock, Rothko, Diebenkorn, de Kooning - given to Stanford by the Anderson family, next door to the Cantor Arts Center.

    Your guide’s note Always free; open Thursday-Monday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday. No reservation needed.

  24. 24 Deep cut within Palo Alto & Stanford

    Xerox PARC

    The low-slung research lab (now PARC, part of SRI International) where the graphical user interface, the mouse, Ethernet, laser printing and WYSIWYG editing were invented in the 1970s - ideas that shaped every modern computer.

    Your guide’s note Exterior/landmark only. It is a working private research facility, not open to the public; the site sits on Coyote Hill above Stanford with hiking-trail views nearby. A pilgrimage for the story, not the building. Viewable from the street/sidewalk only — no public interior access.

    3333 Coyote Hill Rd, Palo Alto, CA 94304

    Recommended by ,

    Bing Concert Hall

    Stanford's acoustically acclaimed 842-seat 'vineyard'-style concert hall, opened in 2013, where audience terraces wrap the stage so no seat sits more than 75 feet from the performers.

    Your guide’s note A performing-arts venue - visitable by attending a Stanford Live concert or event; check the calendar for public performances.

    327 Lasuen St, Stanford, CA 94305

  1. 1 Must see within Mountain View & Los Altos · Chinese

    Chef Chu's

    The definitive Silicon Valley Chinese institution, run by chef Lawrence Chu since 1970 and a stop for heads of state and tech elite; the minced-squab lettuce cups and lemon chicken are the enduring classics.

    1067 N San Antonio Rd, Los Altos, CA 94022

    Recommended by , ,

  2. 2 Must see within Mountain View & Los Altos · Indian

    Sakoon

    Recommended by , ,

  3. 3 Must see within Mountain View & Los Altos

    Google Visitor Experience

    Google's official public front door at the Googleplex, opened October 2023 inside the striking curved 'Gradient Canopy' (Charleston East) building. The rest of the Googleplex is closed to non-employees.

    Your guide’s note Open to the public: the Google Store (hardware + exclusive branded merch), a cafe, the Huddle event space and an outdoor Plaza with public art. Offices and the wider campus are off-limits. Open to visitors.

    2000 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043

    Recommended by ,

  4. 4 Must see within Mountain View & Los Altos

    Computer History Museum

    The world's leading museum of computing history, holding everything from a working Babbage Difference Engine reconstruction to Cray supercomputers and a restored PDP-1. A must for any tech traveler.

    Your guide’s note Fully open to the public (Wed-Sun, ~10a-5p; general admission ~$15). No membership or affiliation needed. Open to visitors.

    1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043

    Recommended by ,

  5. 5 Must see within Mountain View & Los Altos

    Shoreline Amphitheatre

    Northern California's largest outdoor amphitheater, opened in 1986 by Bill Graham, seating about 22,500 between reserved seats and a big grass lawn, next to Shoreline Park by the bay.

    Your guide’s note Open only for concerts, roughly May through October; entry by event ticket. Lawn seating is general admission.

    1 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA 94043

    Recommended by ,

    Zareen's (Mountain View)

  11. 11 Worth the detour within Mountain View & Los Altos

    Steve Jobs' Childhood Home & Apple Garage

    The ranch house where Steve Jobs grew up and where he and Steve Wozniak built the first Apple I computers in the garage in 1976. Los Altos designated it a historic resource in 2013.

    Your guide’s note View from the public street ONLY. It is a private, occupied residence with no plaque or tour; do not enter the property or disturb residents. Just a quiet curbside pilgrimage. Viewable from the street/sidewalk only — no public interior access.

    2066 Crist Dr, Los Altos, CA 94024

  12. 12 Worth the detour within Mountain View & Los Altos

    Android Lawn Statues

    The beloved oversized foam sculptures of Android dessert mascots (Cupcake through Pie, etc.). The tradition ran 2008-2019; newer versions are digital-only.

    Your guide’s note An outdoor photo spot beside the Google Visitor Experience. The statues were moved here from the old Landings Drive lawn (redeveloped) in 2022; the area is technically for Google employees and guests, but visitors are generally welcomed to walk up and photograph them. Best combined with a Visitor Experience stop. Open to visitors.

    Charleston Rd & Huff Ave, Mountain View, CA 94043

    Recommended by ,

  13. 13 Worth the detour within Mountain View & Los Altos

    NASA Ames Exploration Center & Hangar One

    NASA's free space-science visitor center at Ames Research Center/Moffett Field, with Mercury and Apollo-era artifacts, a Mars meteorite and moon-mission exhibits. Nearby looms Hangar One, the colossal 1930s airship hangar that is a Bay Area landmark.

    Your guide’s note The Exploration Center sits outside the security gate and is free and open to the public (Tue-Fri 10a-4p, Sat-Sun 12-4p) - no base access needed. Hangar One and the airfield itself are secured; the hangar is viewable from outside/afar only. (The separate Moffett Field Museum, inside the gate, requires ID and a fee.)

    Moffett Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94035

    Shoreline Park & Lake

    A 750-acre bayfront park built on former landfill, with a 50-acre sailing lake, kite-flying meadows, burrowing owls and miles of paved trails linking to the Bay Trail. The historic Rengstorff House stands near the entrance.

    Your guide’s note Boat and kayak rentals at the lake; Shoreline Amphitheatre concerts can jam parking on show nights.

    3160 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043

    Hobee's

    Your guide’s note Free to stroll; liveliest at the Saturday farmers market and in the evenings. On-street/garage parking nearby.

Cupertino & Saratoga 11 places · area 4 of 7

  1. 1 Must see within Cupertino & Saratoga

    Apple Park Visitor Center

    The public building Apple built across the street from its 'spaceship' ring HQ, opened 2017. A design landmark in its own right, with a carbon-fiber roof floating on stone columns.

    Your guide’s note Open to anyone: full Apple Store, Caffe Macs rooftop cafe/terrace with a distant view over the ring, and an augmented-reality tabletop model of the campus. The ring building itself and the grounds are closed to the public. Open to visitors.

    10600 N Tantau Ave, Cupertino, CA 95014

    Recommended by , , +1,

  2. 2 Must see within Cupertino & Saratoga

    Historic Saratoga Village

    The walkable historic core of Saratoga along Big Basin Way (once 1850s 'Lumber Street'), lined with wine-country-style restaurants, galleries, boutiques and Blaney Plaza. The gateway to Hakone Gardens and Montalvo.

    Your guide’s note Free to wander; parking on Big Basin Way and side lots. Best paired with a nearby garden or winery visit.

    14503 Big Basin Way, Saratoga, CA 95070

    Recommended by ,

  3. 3 Must see within Cupertino & Saratoga

    Rancho San Antonio Preserve

    The South Bay's most popular open space: 24 miles of oak-and-grassland trails, the family-favorite Deer Hollow Farm, and the climb to Wildcat Loop and PG&E Trail. Open 8 a.m. to 30 minutes after sunset.

    Your guide’s note The lot fills by mid-morning on weekends; arrive early or expect to wait.

    22500 Cristo Rey Dr, Cupertino, CA 95014

    Recommended by ,

  4. 4 Must see within Cupertino & Saratoga

    Hakone Estate & Gardens

    One of the oldest Japanese-style residential gardens in the Western Hemisphere (est. 1917), with a koi pond, tea house, bamboo grove and hillside strolling paths. A National Historic District in the Saratoga hills.

    Your guide’s note Paid admission; the Lower House and tea garden are best in spring azalea and fall maple season.

    21000 Big Basin Way, Saratoga, CA 95070

    Recommended by ,

  5. 5 Must see within Cupertino & Saratoga

    Montalvo Arts Center (Villa Montalvo)

    A 1912 Mediterranean-Revival villa built by Senator James Phelan, now an arts center set in 175 hillside acres with formal gardens, an outdoor amphitheater, an artist residency, and free hiking trails through the redwoods.

    Your guide’s note Grounds and trails open daily 8am-sunset, free parking on weekdays; villa interior access varies with events and tours.

    15400 Montalvo Rd, Saratoga, CA 95070

    Recommended by ,

    Your guide’s note Free; open daily 6am to dusk. Saturday open-house and last-Saturday blacksmith demos are the liveliest times.

    Fremont Older Open Space Preserve

    A 739-acre preserve of hayfields, oak woodland and orchard on the Saratoga/Cupertino line, with two lookout peaks (Hunters Point, Maisie's Peak) giving valley-wide views. A favorite of hikers, riders and mountain bikers.

    Your guide’s note Only ~21 spaces at the Prospect Rd lot; go early. Trails are shared with bikes and horses.

    Stevens Creek County Park

    Santa Clara County's first regional park (1924): 1,077 acres of foothills around a 92-acre reservoir, with hiking, fishing, non-motorized boating and links to the Fremont Older and Skyline trails.

    Apple Infinite Loop Campus

    Apple's original headquarters (1993-2017, still active offices/labs) on the private U-shaped street Infinite Loop, the iconic '1 Infinite Loop' address. VIEWABLE ONLY now: the public Apple Company Store that once operated here (exclusive Apple-branded merch you could buy nowhere else) PERMANENTLY CLOSED on Jan 20, 2024, so there is no longer anything open to the public inside.     Intel Museum

    Your guide’s note Free and open to the public inside the Robert Noyce Building lobby (Mon-Fri, ~9a-5p; call ahead as it closes for events). The rest of the Intel campus is not public. Open to visitors.

    A free art museum on El Camino Real focused on Bay Area and California artists, with rotating exhibitions, a permanent collection and a sculpture garden on the grounds. A well-kept Santa Clara secret.

    A working fishing harbor at Princeton-by-the-Sea and the launch point for Mavericks, the legendary big-wave surf break a half-mile offshore where winter swells top 60 feet. Harbor tide pools, seafood shacks and coastal trails round out a day.

    Your guide’s note Harbor free to visit; to glimpse Mavericks, park at the Pillar Point bluff lot and walk the dirt trail. Big-wave season is roughly November-March.

    1 Johnson Pier, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019

    Recommended by ,

  7. 7 Must see within Day Trips & Coast

    Mission Peak (Fremont)

    The Bay Area's most famous foothill summit hike: a relentless ~6-mile round trip climbing 2,000 ft to a 2,517-ft peak and its selfie-famous survey pole, with 360-degree valley and Bay views. A rite of passage for South Bay hikers.

    Your guide’s note Tiny Stanford Ave lot fills at dawn; overflow on Vineyard Ave. Bring water, no shade. Entrance open 6:30 a.m.

    680 Stanford Ave, Fremont, CA 94539

    Recommended by ,

  8. 8 Must see within Day Trips & Coast

    Filoli Historic House & Garden

    A 1917 Georgian country estate on 654 acres in Woodside, with 16 acres of formal English Renaissance gardens, reflecting pools and seasonal displays. A National Trust site open daily 10 a.m.-5 p.m.

    Your guide’s note Paid, often timed-ticket admission; spring tulips and the holiday displays draw crowds. Book ahead.

    86 Canada Rd, Woodside, CA 94062

    Recommended by ,

  9. 9 Must see within Day Trips & Coast

    Big Basin Redwoods State Park

    California's oldest state park (1902) and its old-growth coast redwoods. Badly burned in the 2020 CZU fire, it has reopened for limited day-use with reservations; over 20 miles of trails are restored and the forest is visibly regenerating.

    Your guide’s note Day-use reservations required; a summer weekend/holiday shuttle runs. Full rebuild will take years, so check current access before going.

    21600 Big Basin Way, Boulder Creek, CA 95006

    Recommended by ,

  10. 10 Must see within Day Trips & Coast

    New Museum Los Gatos (NUMU)

    A community art and history museum in downtown Los Gatos with rotating contemporary-art and local-history exhibitions, an easy stop on a day trip to the town's shops and the Los Gatos Creek Trail.

    Your guide’s note Closed Mon-Tue; open Wed-Sun. Free for Los Gatos residents and under-18s; modest admission otherwise.

    106 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030

    Recommended by ,

  11. 11 Must see within Day Trips & Coast · American

    Plumed Horse

    Saratoga's long-running Michelin-starred (18 consecutive years) fine-dining destination, a Silicon Valley special-occasion landmark with a Wine Spectator Grand Award cellar.

    14555 Big Basin Way, Saratoga, CA 95070

    Recommended by ,

  12. 12 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Pulgas Water Temple

    A neoclassical Beaux-Arts temple built by the SFPUC in 1934 to mark where Hetch Hetchy water — piped 160 miles from Yosemite — arrives on the Peninsula, framed by cypress and a long reflecting pool. A striking, little-known monument near Woodside.

    Your guide’s note Free; grounds open weekdays 9am-5pm, and to pedestrians/cyclists on weekends (the parking lot is closed weekends and holidays). Off Cañada Rd near I-280.

    80 Cañada Rd, Redwood City, CA 94062

    Recommended by , ,

  13. 13 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Meta 'Like' Sign, 1 Hacker Way

    The famous sign at the entrance to Meta's (Facebook's) headquarters - once the giant blue thumbs-up 'Like', now the blue Meta infinity logo (swapped in the 2021 rebrand). A classic Silicon Valley selfie stop.

    Your guide’s note Photo stop at the entrance sign ONLY, from the public roadside. The Meta campus is closed to the public - no walk-in access. The famous thumbs-up is gone; the sign now shows the Meta infinity mark (with 'Facebook' still on the reverse). Viewable from the street/sidewalk only — no public interior access.

    1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, CA 94025

    Recommended by ,

  14. 14 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Mystery Spot

    A classic 1940s roadside gravity-illusion attraction in the redwoods above Santa Cruz, where a tilted cabin makes balls appear to roll uphill and people seem to change height. A campy, only-in-California guided tour.

    Your guide’s note Paid timed tours every half hour (~$12), plus $5 cash parking; it sells out midday. Arrive 30 minutes early. Open daily.

    465 Mystery Spot Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95065

    Recommended by ,

  15. 15 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Wilder Ranch State Park

    A coastal state park just north of Santa Cruz combining a preserved 1800s dairy ranch (Victorian farmhouse, adobe, working blacksmith) with bluff-top trails over pocket beaches and tide pools. Popular with hikers and mountain bikers.

    Your guide’s note Day-use parking about $10 (free on foot or bike); park open 8am-sunset, the historic Interpretive Center Thursday-Sunday.

    1401 Coast Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95060

    Recommended by ,

  16. 16 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Roaring Camp Railroads

    A 19th-century-style logging camp in Felton running two heritage trains: an 1890s narrow-gauge steam train that climbs through old-growth redwoods to Bear Mountain, and a diesel line down the San Lorenzo gorge to the Santa Cruz Boardwalk.

    Your guide’s note Paid excursions; gates open 9am-5pm on operating days. Book steam-train tickets ahead, especially for holiday and Thomas events.

    5401 Graham Hill Rd, Felton, CA 95018

    Recommended by ,

  17. 17 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Mount Umunhum Summit

    A 3,486-foot Santa Cruz Mountains peak inside Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve, crowned by 'the Cube' — the concrete base of a Cold War radar tower from the former Almaden Air Force Station. Reopened to the public in 2017 with 360-degree Bay-to-ocean views.

    Your guide’s note Free; reach the summit by the paved Mount Umunhum Rd or a strenuous ~3.7-mile trail from the Bald Mountain lot. The narrow mountain road can close in bad weather — check before going.

    Mount Umunhum Rd, Los Gatos, CA 95033

    Recommended by ,

  18. 18 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Pinnacles National Park

    California's newest national park (2013): the eroded remnants of an ancient volcano, with jagged rock spires, talus caves and one of the best places in the state to spot free-flying California condors. A striking, harder-to-reach day trip southeast of Gilroy.

    Your guide’s note About 1.5-2 hours from San Jose; the east and west entrances are NOT connected by road. Entry fee per vehicle; brutally hot in summer, best in spring. High Peaks Trail is the top condor spot.

    5000 East Entrance Rd, Paicines, CA 95043

    Recommended by ,

  19. 19 Worth the detour within Day Trips & Coast

    Lick Observatory (Mt Hamilton)

    A working University of California observatory on the 4,200-ft summit of Mt Hamilton, reached by a famously winding road with knockout views over San Jose. Free visitor center and tours of the historic 36-inch Great Refractor.

    Your guide’s note Public grounds open weekends noon-5 p.m.; the drive is long and twisty with no gas or food. Check for construction closures.

    7281 Mt Hamilton Rd, Mount Hamilton, CA 95140

    Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park

    An accessible grove of ancient coast redwoods near Felton, with an easy self-guided Redwood Loop, the San Lorenzo River and trails up to an observation deck. A gentler redwood day than Big Basin.

    Your guide’s note Day-use fee; the flat Redwood Loop is stroller-friendly. The Roaring Camp steam railroad runs nearby.

    Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk

    California's classic beachfront amusement park, home to the 1924 wooden Giant Dipper coaster and the 1911 Looff carousel, both National Historic Landmarks. Free to enter, pay per ride; open year-round.

    Your guide’s note Free admission, ride wristbands sold separately; summer weekends are packed and parking is tight.

    400 Beach St, Santa Cruz, CA 95060

    Half Moon Bay State Beach

    Four miles of sandy state beach on the San Mateo coast, edged by the level, paved Coastside Trail running from Pillar Point to Poplar Beach with wide-open ocean views. Day-use 8 a.m. to sunset.

    Your guide’s note Francis Beach is at the end of Kelly Ave; the coast is windy and cold-water, more for walking than swimming.

    95 Kelly Ave, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019

    Your guide’s note Concert season runs spring through fall; entry by event ticket. Gates open ~2 hours before showtime; ~$20 per car parking.

    A horticulture-themed family park in the garlic capital of Gilroy, built around famous 'circus trees' and six gardens with gentle rides and attractions. Seasonal, open roughly late March through early January.

How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (Yelp and TripAdvisor never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. Numbers on the cards match the pins on the map. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

108 sights and 44 places to eat across Palo Alto, Mountain View, Sunnyvale, Cupertino, Santa Clara and San Jose, each traceable to the source that named it. The Valley’s food is its immigrant density — arguably the best Taiwanese, Vietnamese and South Indian eating in the country.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The Valley’s signature strength is immigrant density: Taiwanese (Cupertino/Sunnyvale), Vietnamese (San Jose’s Little Saigon, the largest outside Vietnam), South Indian (Sunnyvale/Milpitas) and the American boba scene the region invented each got a dedicated search led by Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation and the SF Chronicle. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation, SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open.
